newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs issue CZK 1 bln new flood bonds Sept 1.
newsitem.headline: Czechs issue CZK 1 bln new flood bonds Sept 1.

text.p: The Czech Finance Ministry said it would issue a second one billion crown tranche of five-year domestic bonds to pay for flood relief under the same conditions as the first, Finance Minister Ivan Pilip said.

The first tranche was issued with a fixed rate of 12.5 percent for the first year. The final four years of maturity would have an interest rate equal to the average inflation rate for the previous 12 months plus 250 basis points.
"We have decided to make a similar issue on the same conditions, which could be bought from September 1," Pilip told reporters.
The first two tranches are mainly intended for retail investors but Pilip said a third tranche for larger institutions was being considered.
He added that the timing of the issue for institutional investors should be announced by the beginning of September and that further details should be available within 10 days.
Severe flooding last month devastated parts of the east of the Czech Republic. Economists have put the cost at 50-100 billion crowns.
Apart from the flood bonds, the government has pledged some five billion crowns in privatisation proceeds and is considering a loan of more than 10 billion crowns from the European Investment Bank.
